newsitem.title: USA: Civil trial will find him innocent, says Simpson.
newsitem.headline: Civil trial will find him innocent, says Simpson.

text.p: O.J. Simpson, in an interview with CBS to be televised this week, says he will be vindicated at his civil trial and "there'll be retribution" against members of the Los Angeles police and prosecution as a result.

The interview is part of a special to be shown Wednesday night on the CBS News Extra programme "O.J. in Black and White." It was conducted in June before the judge in the civil trial imposed a gag order.

Simpson told CBS correspondent Bill Whitaker, "the best part about this civil case is in many ways I think I'll get vindicated and there'll be retribution." Asked against whom there would be retribution, he said, "Members of the prosecution team and the LAPD (Los Angeles Police department). Members -- not the whole offices." He did not elaborate.

Simpson was found not guilty of murdering his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman at his criminal trial a year ago and now faces a wrongful death civil suit brought by the families of the victims. While he does not face jail time if found guilty, he could be fined millions of dollars.

In the interview, Simpson said his ex-wife was physically abusive to his housekeeper in 1994 and he charged that there was a double standard involved when the issue of his 1989 abuse of Nicole Simpson was raised.
"You can't say that because of an abusive incident in my life that I am now the devil and excuse an abusive incident in Nicole's life," he said.

"(Why is) the black guy dogged and the white girl isn't? I've never looked at things racially but ... evidently they make a distinction: if you're a black male, you're bad, and if you're a white woman, you're not -- for doing the same thing."
